objective.subject: docs: require pull requests for every protected-path change
objective.body:
Two independent reviews of 56f3b8b4 found that its maintainer-approval
exception let an agent push a protected change: the agent writes the commit
body that quotes the approval, so the quote proves nothing. The exception is
removed. Protected paths always go through a pull request, and only the
maintainer pushes them directly.

The same reviews found two more problems, both fixed here:
- The Named branch bullet forbids the separate branch a pull request needs.
  The protected-path bullet now authorizes that branch.
- The bullet restated the integrity job's pull-request-only trigger. It no
  longer does; the rule rests on code-owner review, which the verification
  contract describes.

MUST: a change to a path listed under Protected infrastructure in verification/verification-integrity.md goes through a pull request, which an agent opens on its own branch; only the maintainer pushes such a change directly.
MUST NOT: push a protected-path change directly on any approval an agent records, including one quoted in its own commit body.

Maintainer approval, this session: "optimize this, consider this is my approval" (approves this rule and its optimization).

assurance: SKIPPED. Scope: one bullet in a project-delivery reference, documentation only. It changes no library runtime contract and no behavioral evidence, so no required condition holds.
